sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Dhadkai' (retrieved 2026-09-17); Wikipedia 'Village sign language' and 'List of sign languages'
sources.note: 'Dhadkai' article says residents use a locally developed sign language based on hearing villagers' gestures; cites only news items (Reuters 2009, Al Jazeera 2024, Kashmir Observer 2024) and the medical papers above. The two sign-language list pages do not mention Dadhkai/Dhadkai at all (Indian village SLs listed: Alipur SL, Naga SL).

sources.citation: Kathuria, S. J. & S. Sharma. 2022. The Noisy Silence of Deaf villagers of Dhadkai, Jammu, India: A Case Study. Qeios preprint v2 (23 Nov 2022), 19 pp. doi:10.32388/SD6BEE.2
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Education/social case study by an ISL interpreter; says 'the deaf people of Dhadkai use local sign language and have a very limited vocabulary' and that it is shared by hearing villagers (who speak Gojri and Dogri). No linguistic analysis, no sign inventory, nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Pandey, N., T. Rashid, R. Jalvi, M. Sharma, R. Rangasayee, K. I. Andrabi & A. Anand. 2017. Mutations in OTOF, CLDN14 & SLC26A4 genes as major causes of hearing impairment in Dhadkai village, Jammu & Kashmir, India. Indian J Med Res 146(4): 489-497. doi:10.4103/ijmr.IJMR_635_15
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Molecular genetics; does not mention the sign language at all.

sources.citation: Raina, S. K., M. Saroch, G. Yadav & A. Bhardwaj. 2017. Establishing ancestry through pedigree of a village with high prevalence of hearing-impaired. Journal of Indian Speech Language & Hearing Association 31(1): 1-4. doi:10.4103/jisha.JISHA_15_16
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Epidemiology/pedigree paper; says only 'Dadhkai sign language is commonly used by hearing residents as well as deaf ones till date' and that local field investigators 'were well versed with local sign language'. Nothing on structure or prosody.

sources.citation: Razdan, S., S. K. Raina, K. K. Pandita, S. Razdan, R. Nanda, R. Kaul & S. Dogra. 2012. Inbreeding as a cause for deafness: Dadhkai study. Indian Journal of Human Genetics 18(1): 71-74. doi:10.4103/0971-6866.96655
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Medical genetics paper; only mention of the language (Discussion): 'Dadhkai Sign Language (DSL) is commonly used by hearing residents as well as deaf ones till today.' No linguistic description, nothing on prosody or stress.
